feef40023cdf6a9f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) are considering establishing a control centre to give the police better access to the closed-circuit television (CCTV) system across the federal capital.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the initiative is crucial as about 10,000 CCTV units are installed throughout Kuala Lumpur.
She added that it will enhance operational efficiency in monitoring and responding to security incidents and traffic flow.
“DBKL and the PDRM are indeed in discussions to establish a second command centre that is easily accessible to the Police.

“Currently, although DBKL has smart CCTVs, we rely heavily on the police to be on the ground to ensure smooth traffic flow,” she told reporters after handing over information and communications technology (ICT) equipment at the Sentul District Police Headquarters (IPD) here today.
Hannah, the Segambut MP, said RM60,000 has been allocated for ICT equipment for the front counters of Sentul IPD and three police stations under its administration.
She added that RM100,000 has also been allocated to cover part of the logistics costs for police personnel involved in programmes organised by DBKL.

Hannah said close cooperation between DBKL and the police is vital for managing events in the capital, including road closures for running events and concerts, as well as combating crime and online fraud.
Sentul police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the ICT system will significantly help speed up services to the public, especially when lodging police reports. — Bernama
d75d8f0914ff30f4: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) has appointed four officers to liaise with the families of 54 people who remain missing following flash floods in Nepal, Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (Masfih) said.

Its representative, Dr R. Manivannan, said the appointment was discussed during a two-and-a-half-hour meeting at BNM involving financial institutions, insurance companies and the missing Malaysians' next of kin.

The floods followed the collapse of a mountain and glacier near Nepal's border with China, triggering tsunami-like waves that swept through northern mountainous areas, destroying homes, roads, bridges and settlements.
More than 1,400 people were killed and over 5,000 remain missing.
The four officers will serve as points of contact, reducing the need for families to repeatedly explain their circumstances to different banks, insurers and agencies.
Manivannan said Masfih had requested one additional officer who speaks Tamil and understands the case to improve communication with affected families.
"We have asked for one more officer who is Tamil-speaking and understands the matter so that communication with the affected families can be clearer and more effective," he said.
He said the arrangement would also help protect families from scam calls seeking personal or financial information.
"We want to ensure that they do not fall victim to scam calls or provide sensitive information to people who claim to represent the authorities or financial institutions," he said.
Manivannan said Masfih would continue pressing for measures to address the families' outstanding financial commitments while the status of their missing loved ones remained unresolved.
17ba29399087cbc2: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 12 — Decisions regarding the closure and reopening of schools due to the haze situation will be made periodically based on standard operating procedures (SOPs), existing guidelines, and advice from relevant agencies.

Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said these decisions depend on advice of the Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia) and the Ministry of Health (MOH), as well as the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES).
She noted that the Ministry of Education does not make such decisions in isolation, instead, it takes into account air quality assessments, health advice, and deliberations with relevant committees.
“We have established that we act based on SOPs, existing guidelines, and advice from MET in accordance with periodic directives as well as the Ministry of Health (MOH).
“We have a committee, and we fully adopt the guidelines provided by NRES and the MOH,” she told reporters after attending MOE’s ‘Petah KPM 2026’ programme here today.
Fadhlina said the current haze situation is being monitored according to established guidelines, however, parents must continue to prioritise their children’s health.
She advised parents not to send their children to school if they are unwell, but instead to inform the school of the situation.
“That is why, in the guidance we provide to parents, we state that if children are unwell, they should not be sent to school, and the school should be notified,” she said.

She also expressed appreciation for the cooperation of parents who pay attention to health issues and share their views with the Ministry of Education (MOE), helping the ministry make decisions regarding school management during the haze.
According to her, any decision must strike a balance between protecting students’ health and the impact on education should schools remain closed for an extended period.

Commenting on the possibility of the haze persisting until November or December, Fadhlina said decisions would continue to be made collaboratively, based on the guidelines and advice of relevant agencies.

‘Petah KPM’ serves as a strategic platform to holistically uphold the ‘Upholding the Malay Language and Strengthening the English Language’ (MBMMBI) policy as it emphasises that proficiency in both Malay and English must go hand-in-hand to foster a culture of fluent and courteous communication across diverse ethnic groups. — Bernama
099cb0a13f79b38e: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) coach Xisco Munoz has called on his side to find their clinical edge when they face Pohang Steelers in Tuesday's Asian Champions League Elite (ACLE) clash at the Pohang Steelyard.
Both sides enter matchday two seeking a turnaround after disappointing openers.
Pohang, three-time Asian champions from South Korea, were beaten 3-1 by Beijing FC, while the Southern Tigers were held to a 1-1 draw by Buriram United at Sultan Ibrahim Stadium last month.
Munoz warned his squad that controlling possession means nothing without sharp finishing in the final third.

"In the ACLE, the only difference is in the last third. Last season at Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, we played well to beat Pohang Steelers 5-2 despite trailing 1-0. Now it is our turn to play at their home ground, which will certainly pose a tough challenge against a Korean club," said Munoz.
"In the ACLE, we must give our full focus and attention. We must be ready for every situation, both in attack and defence.
"It will be a tough and intense match, but we need 100 per cent focus and our best performance to record a positive result so we can stay competitive in the tournament."
The Spanish coach confirmed defensive midfielder Eddy Israfilov will miss the match as he serves a two-game suspension following a red card against Thailand's Buriram United on Sept 15.
However, Munoz expressed confidence in his squad's ability to contain Pohang's forward line.

"We must keep a strong mindset and work hard to achieve our goal. We came to South Korea to claim all three points, and the players must embrace this challenge even though it will be difficult," he said.

"There are two or three tactical setups the opposition might employ, particularly in attack, so we must be tactically solid to play safely and comfortably when attacking their defensive third while neutralising their dominance.
"We will see how the match unfolds. JDT always play with a winning mentality, and the 90 minutes on the pitch will decide everything," Munoz added.
Tuesday's clash marks the fourth continental meeting between the two teams.
While Pohang won their initial encounters in 2021 (4-1 and 2-0), JDT secured a 5-2 win during their most recent meeting in the 2024-2025 edition.
The hosts enter the match on a three-match losing streak in the ACLE, while JDT have struggled on the road, losing four of their last five away fixtures in the competition.

JDT reached the round of 16 in 2022 and 2024-2025, before achieving their best continental run last season (2025-2026) by reaching the quarter-finals, where they lost 2-1 to eventual champions Al-Ahli.
03028332f8096cc0: KUALA LUMPUR: Sebuah kumpulan mewakili waris 54 rakyat Malaysia yang hilang dalam bencana banjir di Nepal telah mengemukakan cadangan kepada Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) bagi mewujudkan rangka kerja perlindungan kewangan berstruktur untuk membela nasib keluarga mangsa.
Jurucakap kumpulan R Manivannan berkata, cadangan itu memperincikan penyelesaian berkaitan perlindungan liabiliti, pemeliharaan aset, dan kesinambungan perniagaan.
Satu dokumen berasingan setebal 20 muka surat turut diserahkan kepada wakil persatuan perbankan, kewangan dan takaful.

Selepas pertemuan dengan pegawai BNM selesai, Manivannan memaklumkan bahawa institusi kewangan pada dasarnya bersetuju menangguhkan usaha kutipan hutang sementara menunggu garis panduan rasmi dimuktamadkan.

"Secara dasarnya, semua pihak bersetuju buat masa ini tiada sebarang tindakan akan diambil sehingga kata sepakat dicapai. Mereka tidak akan tuntut bayaran daripada pihak keluarga," katanya kepada pemberita di luar bangunan Institut Bank-Bank Bertauliah Asia (AICB) hari ini.

Menerusi rangka kerja yang dicadangkan itu, kumpulan terbabit menuntut bank memberikan moratorium pinjaman penuh dengan pengecualian jelas terhadap faedah terakru, penalti bayaran lewat, serta pelanjutan tempoh pembiayaan secara arbitrari.
Manivannan bagaimanapun tidak mendedahkan kandungan lain dokumen cadangan itu.

Beliau berkata, status mangsa yang belum ditemukan meletakkan waris dalam ketidaktentuan dari segi undang-undang sehingga menyukarkan mereka mengakses akaun bank, pelaburan, mahupun polisi insurans berikutan sijil kematian tidak dapat dikeluarkan oleh mahkamah tanpa pengesahan penemuan mayat.

Bagaimanapun, beliau berkata, keputusan terkini Nepal yang membenarkan mangsa dianggap meninggal dunia selepas 45 hari hilang berbanding tempoh 12 tahun sebelum ini dijangka mempercepat penyelesaian isu tersebut, memandangkan tempoh berkenaan telah pun berlalu.
b6c23e8b22f64758: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The High Court today fixed June 14, 2027, for case management of the Malaysian Bar’s judicial review application challenging the prosecution’s decision to discontinue the Yayasan Akalbudi corruption case involving Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.

Judge S. Indra Nehru set the date after lawyer Abhilaash Subramaniam, representing the Malaysian Bar, informed the court that Ahmad Zahid and the Attorney-General (AG) had obtained leave from the Federal Court on Oct 8 to appeal against an earlier Court of Appeal ruling.
“We therefore request that the judicial review hearing at the High Court be held after the Federal Court appeal proceedings are concluded,” Abhilaash said during case management.
The court also directed that the next case management be conducted via e-review before a High Court deputy registrar.

Abhilaash also informed the court that no date had been fixed for the substantive appeal hearing, adding that preparations, including compiling the appeal records and exchanging written submissions, could take several months.
Federal counsel Safiyyah Omar, representing the AG, agreed to the proposal, while Ahmad Zahid’s lawyer, Datuk Guok Ngek Seong, raised no objection.

On Oct 8, a three-member Federal Court panel led by Chief Judge of Malaya Datuk Seri Hashim Hamzah granted Ahmad Zahid and the AG leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision allowing the Malaysian Bar to initiate judicial review proceedings.

Hashim, sitting with Federal Court judges Datuk Nordin Hassan and Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali, ruled that the case raised novel constitutional questions of public importance requiring clarification and a definitive ruling by the Federal Court.
On May 7, the Court of Appeal granted the Malaysian Bar leave to challenge the AG’s decision on Sept 4, 2023, to discontinue proceedings against Ahmad Zahid.
The appellate court overturned a June 27, 2024, High Court ruling that had dismissed the Malaysian Bar’s application for leave to commence judicial review.

Ahmad Zahid, named as the proposed second respondent in the judicial review, subsequently applied for leave to appeal to the Federal Court on May 25. AG Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar filed a separate application.

In its judicial review application, the Malaysian Bar seeks a High Court declaration that the decision by then High Court judge Datuk Collin Lawrence Sequerah, now a Federal Court judge, to grant Ahmad Zahid a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA) on 47 charges of criminal breach of trust, corruption and money laundering linked to Yayasan Akalbudi was null and void.
The High Court granted the DNAA after the prosecution informed the court that the AG Chambers intended to discontinue the proceedings to examine new evidence. — Bernama
e16a6d39f66d7251: BRUSSELS, Oct 12 — The European Union will cap imports of hybrid vehicles from China to 350,000 a year, a senior EU official said today, after Brussels and Beijing agreed to moderate such exports.
“This will cut by more than half the current exports to the EU, which we estimate are likely to reach up to 800,000 units in 2026,” the official said. — AFP
62cce3e90d388dc8: PESHAWAR: Pakistani authorities have detained hundreds of members of jailed former prime minister Imran Khan's party after emergency rule was imposed in a northern province, police officials told AFP on Monday.

Two police officials, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak to the media, said 278 members of Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party had been detained in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province since Sunday's emergency declaration.

The PTI-ruled province was placed under emergency rule following days-long anti-government protests demanding Khan's release, while militant violence in the area has also been mounting, particularly along the border with Afghanistan.
Thousands of Khan's supporters have been marching in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, also airing anti-government grievances fuelled by harsh economic conditions.

The hugely popular former cricket star's party said on Sunday the province's chief minister Sohail Afridi had been arrested hours after the extraordinary constitutional measures were announced by Pakistan's presidency.
An administrative official, also speaking on condition of anonymity, told AFP that Afridi had been placed in "protective custody" in his official residence but later moved to another location.
The official declined to disclose the new location.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa is a stronghold for Khan's party, and the PTI-led government there would be "non-functional" until the security situation improves, the government said.
Islamabad has accused the PTI administration in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa of failing to deal with the militants, necessitating the imposition of emergency rule.
The PTI has vehemently opposed the constitutional measures, describing them as undemocratic and a grab for power by the federal government.
Khan has been behind bars since August 2023, facing scores of charges ranging from corruption to inciting violence, following widespread anti-establishment riots in May that year.
He and his legal team reject the allegations, branding them as politically motivated.
a3c358dd0914ff1d: KATHMANDU: More than 100 foreign trekkers are stranded at different locations after the flooding of a river in central Nepal at the weekend swept away hiking trails and bridges, an official said on Monday.

Authorities rescued 96 people including nine foreigners after a landslide on Sunday in Gorkha district, about 100 km (62 miles) west of Kathmandu, blocked ​the Budhi Gandaki River, leading to downstream flooding.

The river is ​a tributary of the Trishuli River, downstream from another tributary where a glacier collapse caused a catastrophic flood in August that killed 1,457 people, with thousands still missing.
The army said the latest rescue operation was continuing on Monday even as the flood has receded.

There were no reports of fatalities, but five villagers are out of contact after the flooded river carrying black muddy sludge and debris washed away homes and damaged infrastructure including three hydroelectric plants, national disaster authorities said.

Bhuwan Raj Ojha, an official of the Manaslu Conservation Area Project (MACP) that includes a popular trekking route, said there were more than 100 foreign trekkers stranded in different areas who could not return because part of the trail had been swept away.
"Those hikers who want to return because of the flood need to be rescued. Those who want to continue their trekking can do so from locations that are safe," Ojha told Reuters from Gorkha.
"There are restaurants and tea houses along the route. They are safe."

The International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said the latest flood may have been triggered by the failure of a temporary river blockage created by a landslide, according to preliminary accounts from Nepal's authorities reviewed by ICIMOD.
"This event is another reminder of how exposed mountain communities and river corridors remain to sudden, cascading hazards," Pema Gyamtsho, director general of ICIMOD, said.
"While response efforts must remain the immediate priority, understanding what triggered this flood will be critical for reducing future risks and strengthening resilience."
df1f7a19040c9ce7: KUALA LUMPUR: Filled with joy for Bella Astillah and Syed Saddiq following their wedding, actress Nadia Brian admitted that the couple's heartwarming nuptials have renewed her faith in true love and reignited her hopes of finding happiness herself.
Nadia, 35, remarked that everyone's romantic journey is unique and said past heartbreak should never be a reason to close one's heart to new beginnings.

"Seeing Bella Astillah and Syed Saddiq get married made me believe that true love really does exist. There are still good, responsible men out there who can make their partners genuinely happy," she said in a recent news report.
"Some of us may be unlucky in love, but that doesn't mean we are destined to fail forever. There is always a rainbow after the rain—it's just a matter of time.
"Most importantly, as women, we must know our self-worth, continually improve ourselves, and work on our shortcomings. God willing, good things will come at the right time."

The Bisik Asmara star added that life's trials and failed relationships should be seen as valuable lessons that help shape a person into someone who is more mature, resilient, and wiser when choosing a partner.
She noted that seeing her friends happy gives her the encouragement to keep trusting in life's plan, even if she has yet to meet her own soulmate.
"I also hope that one day I'll be blessed with happiness and meet the right partner—a man who can guide, nurture, and complement me," she shared.
"Seeing my friends happy gives me hope that God has written the best story for each of us. What matters most is that we never lose faith in goodness and love."
On Saturday morning, the popular couple—affectionately dubbed 'BASS' by fans—officially tied the knot in a deeply meaningful ceremony at around 10.40 am.
During the ceremony, Syed Saddiq presented seven hantaran (wedding gift trays) to Bella, while the bride reciprocated with nine trays.

Among the standout gifts that caught the public's attention were a custom gold ornament shaped like Mount Kinabalu, an Umrah pilgrimage package, an EPF (Employees Provident Fund) contribution of RM100,000, and a bicycle.
ffc2d13ad670fb7c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin today alleged that the government’s hybrid taxation proposal was tacit admission that it was wrong to reject the goods and services tax (GST).

While debating the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027, Hamzah said recent proposals to incorporate elements of the consumption tax into the existing Sales and Service Tax (SST) also indicated that the latter system was lacking.
“If you want the GST, just implement the GST. Don’t leave the people waiting in uncertainty,” Hamzah said.
“This looks like it’s heading in that direction, but no one wants to actually say they want to use the GST.”
He alleged that Pakatan Harapan lawmakers in the government now were “embarrassed” to support reviving the GST due to their rejection of it previously.

First implemented at a standard rate of six per cent in April 2015 under former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, the broad-based consumption tax became a central battleground in Malaysian electoral politics.
Following its historic victory in the 2018 general election, the PH administration zero-rated the GST before repealing it in favour of the current SST regime.
e4b28358b320d156: RIYADH, Oct 12 — Saudi Arabia’s energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman today said recent developments required a serious response, in remarks made after multiple fatal attacks by the Houthis on Riyadh airport and across the kingdom.
“The events of recent weeks are serious, our response must be equally serious,” the minister told an energy conference in Riyadh. — AFP
41e254d71bc037de: KUALA LUMPUR: National track riders competing at the Shanghai World Championships on Oct 14-18 will have to adapt quickly to conditions at the Shanghai Velodrome, China's new flagship indoor track.
National track cycling head coach (sprints) Harnizam Basri said nobody in the squad has experienced racing there before.
"We have no experience racing here as this is the first time they are having a (major international) competition here," said Harnizam recently.
"We don't have any data from this track. We have had a number of training sessions on the track so far and have been working out the best way to do a flying lap here.
"I guess the most important aspect is the gearing, we have to select the right gears."
Harnizam added that the track does have some similarities to the famous Izu Velodrome in Japan, where the squad raced during the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games last month, but described it as "heavier".
"Its characteristics do share some similarities with the Izu Velodrome, it is also a 7.5 metre wide track and has banking of 45 degrees," he said.
"But the conditions are a bit heavier as it is a sea-level track, the barometric pressure is over 1,000 hPa, Izu was only about 900 hpa."
The Shanghai Velodrome, officially opened in May 2024, is situated on Chongming Island.
The facility also serves as a UCI World Cycling Centre (WCC) Continental Development Satellite.

The world championships is set to begin on Wednesday with Malaysian riders set to compete in the men's team sprint (Shah Firdaus Sahrom, Ridwan Sahrom, Fadhil Zonis, Akmal Jusena) and women's team sprint (Izzah Izzati Asri, Nur Alyssa Farid, Aliana Azizan, Anis Amira Rosidi).
Former world keirin champion Azizulhasni Awang will take to the track for the men's keirin on Thursday.
d9301a54359e04b2: PETALING JAYA: Sultan Selangor Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah mahu perancangan projek sisa kepada tenaga (WTE) di negeri itu diteruskan dan disegerakan dengan bantuan kerajaan Persekutuan.

Menurut kenyataan Istana Alam Shah, baginda berharap kerajaan Persekutuan dapat mempermudahkan proses pembangunan kemudahan itu yang bukan sahaja mampu mengurangkan pencemaran terhadap alam sekitar selain mengatasi masalah tapak pelupusan sanitari semakin terhad.

Kenyataan itu berkata Sultan Sharafuddin berharap pemeteraian Akta Pengurusan Sisa Pepejal dan Pembersihan Awam 2007 (Akta 672) membabitkan tiga pihak dapat memberi manfaat dan memastikan tahap pengurusan sisa pepejal dan pembersihan awam berada pada paras lebih baik.

"Baginda turut menegaskan selepas perjanjian ini ditandatangani, tidak ada sebarang kompromi serta kemerosotan dari segi prestasi dan kualiti perkhidmatan pengurusan sisa dan pembersihan awam, termasuk dari segi ketepatan masa dan frekuensi kutipan.
"Baginda juga berharap agar perancangan waste-to-energy (WTE) di Selangor dapat diteruskan dan disegerakan melalui pemudahcaraan bersesuaian oleh kerajaan Persekutuan dalam tempoh terdekat," katanya.

Baginda menerima menghadap Menteri Perumahan dan Kerajaan Tempatan Nga Kor Ming pada 8 Okt dan Menteri Besar Amirudin Shari serta Setiausaha Kerajaan Selangor Ahmad Fadzli Ahmad Tajuddin bagi membincangkan hal berkaitan.
Hasrat itu disuarakan baginda susulan lawatannya ke WTE Amager Bakke (CopenHill) di Copenhagen, Denmark, bulan lalu.
Amager Bakke dibangunkan berteraskan konsep yang menggabungkan kecekapan industri, kelestarian alam sekitar dan kesejahteraan masyarakat.
Loji itu berupaya memproses kira-kira 400,000 tan sisa setahun untuk menghasilkan bekalan elektrik serta sistem pemanasan daerah kepada puluhan ribu kediaman di Copenhagen.
27e0dab93a7b7f5b: HONG KONG, Oct 12 — Stock markets were mixed today as oil prices fell after Donald Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, which offset a fresh wave of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Both main crude contracts sank more than one per cent at one point following the US president’s declaration, even as it sparked astonishment in Kyiv, which also said Moscow had struck multiple power plants in the country.
“Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine,” Trump said early yesterday on Truth Social. “Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!”

His post came after he called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to halt attacks on Russian refineries and said it was “time for Ukraine to get a new president” who would finally settle the war.
Zelensky appeared to express surprise at the announcement, saying he was seeking further details, but added that “Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well”.
Russia has yet to confirm its agreement.

While the announcement was welcomed by Ukraine’s allies, Trump had come under fire after declaring a temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian diesel, which European leaders and Kyiv said would only embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin.
The drop in oil prices reversed an initial spike that came in response to Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia at the weekend.

At least a dozen people were killed at Riyadh’s international airport on Saturday — the deadliest attack on Saudi soil for more than a decade — and another person died following a second strike yesterday.
The assaults marked a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh has long militarily supported the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
The Iran-backed group yesterday claimed multiple attacks over the past 24 hours and threatened to keep targeting the kingdom’s transit hubs, calling them “a theatre of operations for our forces”.
“The market is no longer paying full geopolitical premium on every headline, and that is probably the most useful signal in the morning price action,” wrote SPI Asset Management’s Stephen Innes.

“A strike matters if it threatens real barrels, shipping lanes, refining capacity or insurance costs; otherwise, the market is getting increasingly reluctant to pay up simply because the geopolitical ticker flashes red.
“The physical market remains tight enough to keep Brent above US$100 (RM403), but futures are refusing to treat every new escalation as the start of another straight-line inflation shock.”
Asian markets enjoyed a healthy start to the day, but the rally petered as the day wore on.
Hong Kong, Sydney, Singapore, Wellington and Manila all rose, but Seoul and Taipei were dragged by losses in chipmakers SK hynix, Samsung and TSMC.
There were also losses in Shanghai, Mumbai, Bangkok and Jakarta.
US futures were sharply higher, while London, Frankfurt and Paris opened higher.
Tokyo was closed for a holiday.

Investors are also gearing up for the release of key US inflation and retail sales data, which could play a big role in the Federal Reserve’s decision-making regarding interest rates. The bank is due to meet at the end of October.
Also in view is the beginning of earnings season this week, with banking giants JP Morgan, Goldman Sachs and Bank of America due to report.
Tech giants will follow later in the month and November, with traders keen to get an idea on the outlook for the AI sector in light of the vast sums of cash pumped into it in recent years. — AFP
6bd9a24fb7a8dc74: KUALA LUMPUR: Seorang buruh binaan yang sebelum ini berdepan pertuduhan menculik warga Palestin, dijatuhi hukuman penjara tiga tahun oleh Mahkamah Tinggi kerana melarikan dan mengurung lelaki terbabit di sebuah chalet, empat tahun lalu.
Hakim Mohd Arief Emran Arifin menjatuhkan hukuman itu terhadap Edy Ko'im Said, 46, selepas tertuduh mengaku bersalah atas pertuduhan pilihan melarikan dan mengurung lelaki warga Palestin itu.
Mahkamah memerintahkan bapa kepada tiga anak itu menjalani hukuman pemenjaraan bermula hari ini.

Mengikut pertuduhan pilihan, Edy Ko'im didakwa melarikan secara paksa mangsa berusia 31 tahun dengan niat hendak mengurungnya secara rahsia dan salah di Jalan Mayang, Dang Wangi, di sini, pada 10.40 malam, 28 Sept 2022.
Dia dituduh mengikut Seksyen 365 Kanun Keseksaan yang memperuntukkan hukuman penjara maksimum tujuh tahun dan boleh dikenakan denda.

Berdasarkan fakta kes, warga Palestin berkenaan dilarikan sebelum dikurung di sebuah chalet di Hulu Langat, Selangor sebelum diselamatkan polis dalam satu serbuan berpandukan maklumat risikan dan menjumpai mangsa dengan keadaan tangan serta kakinya diikat menggunakan pengikat kabel.

Terdahulu, Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Mahadhir Mohd Khairudin memaklumkan kepada mahkamah bahawa sebelum ini tertuduh didakwa atas pertuduhan menculik, namun representasinya diterima dan pertuduhan pilihan ditawarkan terhadapnya.
"Pihak kami mohon supaya tertuduh dikenakan hukuman penjara yang sewajarnya dengan mengambil kira kesalahan dilakukan adalah serius," katanya.
Peguam Kelvinder Singh Sidhu yang mewakili Edy Ko'im memohon hukuman penjara minimum kerana anak guamnya perlu menyara isteri serta tiga anak.

Sementara itu, kes culik mangsa sama yang dihadapi tujuh lagi tertuduh iaitu Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 45, Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 45, Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 46, Muhammad Iqmal Abdul Rahis, 31, Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 60, Nidarahayu Zainal, 40, Raibafie Amdan, 45 diteruskan dengan perbicaraan hari ini.

Mengikut pertuduhan, semua tertuduh dengan niat bersama menahan mangsa di lokasi dan waktu yang sama untuk mendapatkan ganjaran, iaitu rahsia maklumat membuat dan menyahaktifkan perisian komputer yang digunakan bagi menggodam telefon bimbit.

Kelapan-lapan individu berkenaan didakwa mengikut Seksyen 3 Akta Penculikan 1961 dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 Kanun Keseksaan yang membawa hukuman penjara minimum 30 tahun dan maksimum 40 tahun serta sebatan, jika sabit kesalahan.

Selain kes culik, Tengku Arif Bongsu dan pasangan suami isteri iaitu Nidarahayu serta Raibafie turut berdepan 19 pertuduhan pengubahan wang haram membabitkan nilai melebihi RM250,000 mengikut Seksyen 4(1)(b) Akta Pencegahan Pengubahan Wang Haram, Pencegahan Pembiayaan Keganasan dan Hasil Daripada Aktiviti Haram (AMLATFPUAA) 2001.

Pada 10 Julai 2025, enam lelaki iaitu Mohamad Norakmal Hassan, 46, Mohd Azwan Jamaludin, 42, Dody Junaidi, 47, Mohamad Sufian Saly, 28, Tengku Hazarul Ismail Tengku Hamid, 54 dan Muhammad Al Hatim Mohd Fauzi, 28, dipenjara lima tahun selepas mengaku salah atas pertuduhan pilihan kerana melarikan dan mengurung mangsa sama.
13541111ad044a84: KUALA LUMPUR: OSK Group is targeting RM1.34 billion in property launches in 2027 as it strengthens its focus on higher-end residential projects, recurring property income and a more active construction tender strategy under a refreshed brand direction.
The group unveiled a refreshed identity for its three key business divisions - OSK Construction, OSK Property Investment and OSK Property Development - collectively represented as CID.
OSK deputy group managing director Ong Ju Xing said the refresh was more than a visual change, reflecting the group's ambitions for its next phase of growth.

"'Making Ordinary Extraordinary' gives us a common purpose and reminds us that ordinary people like us can create extraordinary outcomes when we have a shared purpose to improve the everyday experiences that matter to the lives we touch," he said.

Ong said the group is entering the next chapter with optimism by bringing together the strengths of CID, combined with its cables manufacturing, industrialised building system (IBS) wall panel manufacturing, and hospitality businesses.
"We believe we can create even greater value for our customers, business partners and the communities we serve," he said in a statement.

OSK Property development plans to launch projects with a combined gross development value of RM1.34 billion in 2027, expanding its residential portfolio across market segments and locations, including an entry into the high-end residential segment in Subang under its Signature series.
The planned Subang development is expected to complement OSK Property's existing residential offerings as it seeks to cater to changing homebuyer preferences and a broader range of customers.
New launches will include OSK Ombak in Kuantan, the first project under the Signature series, whose first phase was fully booked within three months, according to the group.
Meanwhile, OSK Property Investment will focus on strengthening the lifestyle and community appeal of its existing assets, including Atria Shopping Gallery, Faber Towers and YOUCity Retail.
The strategy involves developing a broader mix of retail, dining, wellness, leisure and community experiences.
OSK Construction, in turn, will embark on a more active growth strategy by increasing its participation in tenders for external construction projects.
62f9235a9af3a40b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — U Mobile, Malaysia’s best 5G network provider, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with HLGY Energy Sdn Bhd to collaborate on the development of next-generation smart solar farm solutions in Malaysia, enabled by U Mobile’s ULTRA5G network. The collaboration brings together private 5G connectivity, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and industrial automation to enhance the monitoring and management of solar farm operations.

HLGY Energy is a Malaysian renewable energy developer focused on developing and operating utility-scale solar and integrated energy solutions under Malaysia’s Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS) framework, including the Kedah Rubber City Solar Power Plant.

Under the MoU, both companies will explore the deployment of a private 5G network that would form the digital backbone of the smart solar farm. U Mobile would serve as HLGY Energy’s innovation, automation and communications infrastructure provider. The network’s dedicated, secure and reliable connectivity would support applications including autonomous drone inspections, AI-powered analytics and smart CCTV surveillance, enabling remote monitoring, earlier issue detection and faster response to operational and maintenance needs.

The partnership supports U Mobile’s enterprise growth strategy by applying the capabilities of its ULTRA5G network to the evolving needs of the renewable energy sector. Its network capabilities have received independent recognition by Ookla and Opensignal for speed and availability. The collaboration also strengthens U Mobile’s role as a digital solutions partner supporting businesses in their digital transformation.

“This collaboration will demonstrate how U Mobile’s ULTRA5G network can enable the next generation of smart and sustainable infrastructure. By combining private 5G connectivity with AI and industrial automation, we aim to help HLGY Energy develop renewable energy assets that are safer, more efficient and increasingly autonomous,” How Lih Ren, Chief Business Officer of U Mobile, said.

“Beyond connectivity, our ambition is to be a trusted digital solutions partner to enterprises across Malaysia. We look forward to applying our network and technology capabilities to support the country’s renewable energy aspirations, including the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS).”

“Malaysia’s green energy transition needs renewable energy infrastructure that is reliable, efficient and built for the future. Our collaboration with U Mobile brings together solar energy expertise and private 5G connectivity to explore how AI and automation can improve the way we operate and manage our solar assets,” Kenneth Yap, Chairman and Executive Director of HLGY Energy, said.

“Integrating AI with solar generation and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) operations can optimise when energy is stored and supplied, help reduce electricity costs and extend equipment life. As we advance our ambitions under CRESS, we aim to make clean energy a dependable choice for businesses, helping Malaysian industries decarbonise and contributing to the nation’s sustainable growth.”

The initiative supports HLGY Energy’s longer-term renewable energy plans including opportunities under CRESS. It demonstrates how advanced connectivity and automation can transform the management of critical energy infrastructure.

The collaboration reflects the growing convergence between digital infrastructure and renewable energy, demonstrating how advanced connectivity and intelligent technologies can support the digitalisation of Malaysia’s energy infrastructure.

Enterprises interested in learning more about U Mobile’s private 5G and smart infrastructure solutions or exploring collaboration opportunities across renewable energy and other critical infrastructure sectors, can visit U Business for more information.
7978bf85d13450a5: KOTA TINGGI: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) suspects vandalism at its substation along Jalan Besar Felda Adela, where a man was found dead early today.
In a statement, TNB said its technical team was sent to the site after receiving a report of an electrical accident involving a member of the public on Oct 12.
"The incident is believed to be linked to vandalism. TNB will provide full support and cooperation to the authorities in their investigations," it said.
TNB also warned the public against tampering with or approaching electrical installations, saying this could result in serious injury or death.
Earlier, Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police received a report at 6.46am of an unconscious man at Km 21 of the road towards Sungai Rengit.

Several tools, including a hoe, cordless grinder, metal hammer, pipe wrench and headlamp, were found nearby.
