face278ad2d9520b: SEPANG, Oct 12 — Malaysians are advised to temporarily postpone travel to Saudi Arabia for Umrah following security concerns after a deadly attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said.

He said that while there had been no incident in Makkah, the missile attack in Riyadh had prompted the government to advise Malaysians to defer non-essential travel to Makkah and Madinah for the time being.

“There has been no incident in Makkah, but the missile explosion in Riyadh has raised security concerns,” he told reporters after attending the departure of Jordan’s King Abdullah II at the Bunga Raya Complex here today

Yesterday, the Foreign Ministry reported that no Malaysians had been killed or injured in Saturday’s attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh or the incident involving a projectile that fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.
Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that the attack on King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people and injured 309 others.
The fatalities comprised four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis and one national each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan. — Bernama
ba44a6132f345bf7: Raspberry Pi Desktop has returned after four years, skipping Debian 12 to deliver a new version based on Debian 13 "Trixie." The updated release brings the familiar Pi desktop to PCs and Intel Macs, and could be worth a look if you want a simple, lightweight Linux to revive an older machine. Raspberry Pi's main business is making and selling its relatively inexpensive Arm single-board computers. This isn't its only activity, though: as well as hardware, it also maintains its own custom Debian-based distro. Although we've covered a few alternative Pi distros over the years, we suspect that most Pi owners never try anything other than the official Pi OS. Pi OS is Debian, but heavily cut down so that it doesn't use much memory or disk space. Its custom desktop grew out of LXDE and was initially presented as PIXEL. It doesn't get much coverage, but for a decade now, there's also been a version for x86 PCs and Intel Macs, offering a similar desktop experience without the bundled version of Mathematica. We covered the last major update to the Raspberry Pi Desktop when the company released a new Debian 11-based version in the middle of 2022. Debian "Bullseye" was released in 2021, and as the Raspberry Pi Desktop is based directly on it, it still got updates for years thereafter, but its Long Term Support coverage ended on August 31. In 2023, Pi OS 5 arrived, based on Debian 12 and with a fancy new Wayland-based desktop, but sadly, no x86 PC version ever joined it. Once Debian 13 got to its first point release, along came Pi OS 6 in October 2025. A year later, the PC edition has caught up. It has the same Wayland-based desktop, complete with the Raspberry Pi Connect remote-control service. The other major change is that the PC edition is now x86-64 only, supporting compatible PCs and Intel Macs but not Apple Silicon models. Existing users will need a fresh installation rather than an in-place upgrade from the old 32-bit release. We haven't had a chance to test it yet, but plan to come back for a deeper look fairly soon. ®
d3b8ebd43973e2a5: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across multiple states, forecasting heavy rain, lightning, and gusty winds in parts of Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak, Sabah, and the Federal Territory of Labuan until 6pm today.
The adverse weather advisory, issued at 3pm this afternoon, takes effect ahead of the evening peak traffic hours.

In the northern and eastern regions of the peninsula, the warning encompasses Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, and Selama), Kelantan (Jeli and Gua Musang), and Terengganu (Dungun, Hulu Terengganu, and Kemaman).
Pahang faces widespread exposure across ten districts: Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Jerantut, Bentong, Temerloh, Maran, Kuantan, Pekan, and Rompin.

Further south, the alert covers Hulu Langat and Sepang in Selangor, alongside the Federal Territory of Putrajaya. In Negeri Sembilan, stormy weather is expected across Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau, and Kuala Pilah.
In Johor, the affected southern corridor includes Kulai, Pontian, Kota Tinggi, and Johor Bahru.
In East Malaysia, the advisory covers northern Sarawak, specifically Limbang and the Bario highlands in Miri.

In Sabah, the warning covers extensive territory across five divisions: Kudat, the West Coast, the Interior (Tambunan, Sipitang, Beaufort, Membakut, Keningau, Tenom, and Kuala Penyu), Tawau (specifically Lahad Datu), and Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Paitan). The Federal Territory of Labuan has also been placed on alert.

MetMalaysia explained that a thunderstorm warning is triggered when cloud formations show signs of imminent heavy rainfall with an intensity exceeding 20 millimetres per hour, or when storms are expected to last for more than an hour.
The department emphasized that these advisories serve as short-term alerts and remain valid for a maximum duration of six hours from the time of issuance.

Members of the public, particularly motorists travelling through affected corridors, are advised to exercise heightened caution on slippery roads, steer clear of flood-prone lowlands, and monitor official meteorological updates for real-time adjustments.
089931b0fc4c35b6: BEIJING: China condemned on Monday recent attacks by the Houthis on Saudi airports and energy infrastructure, expressing "serious concern" about the conflict between Riyadh and the Yemeni group intensifying.
"China condemns the attacks that caused heavy casualties and expresses serious concern over the intensification of the conflict," foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told a regular briefing.

"We call on relevant parties to avoid taking actions that escalate regional tensions, to resolve differences and disputes through dialogue and negotiation, and to achieve peace and stability in the region at an early date," Mao said.

A Houthi strike hit Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, killing one person and wounding 11, a day after another deadly attack claimed by the Iran-backed group forced a suspension of operations there.

Saturday's attack, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, was a sharp escalation in the Yemen war, where Riyadh has long militarily supported the internationally recognised government against the Houthis.
The Houthis have stepped up their attacks on the Riyadh airport - where three people were also killed on Thursday - as well as on Saudi oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
362d8390f7231c35: KUALA LUMPUR: Can Malaysia make Formula One lucrative enough to justify a permanent return to the Sepang International Circuit?

That is the question posed by BA of Malaysia president Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz, who is also Malaysian Investment Development Authority (MIDA) chairman, following his visit to the recent Singapore Grand Prix.

Weighing the commercial realities against the motorsport prestige of hosting the race, Tengku Zafrul said any future bid must look beyond the track action and assess whether the economic returns justify the hosting costs.
"Singapore is truly remarkable in turning F1 into not just a race, but a complete experience," Tengku Zafrul said on X.

"From hospitality and entertainment to the atmosphere surrounding the race, everything is world-class. They also organise conferences and business events on the sidelines of F1, making it a platform to build relationships and open up economic opportunities."
Tengku Zafrul, who is also a former finance minister, said while Malaysia holds a technical edge in terms of track layout, an event's financial blueprint remains paramount.
"At the same time, many drivers and F1 fans still regard Sepang as among the most challenging circuits in the F1 world," he said.
"High-speed corners, unpredictable weather, and a track design that truly tests a driver's skill — it is truly a circuit built for pure racing!

"We already have a world-class circuit. But to bring F1 back, we must think beyond just the race. How do we attract tourists, generate revenue, and ensure the economic returns are worth the hosting costs?
"The big question: can we make F1 profitable enough for Malaysia?"
Malaysia was a regular fixture on the F1 calendar from 1999 until 2017.
Talk of a permanent return to Sepang has gained traction after the circuit made an impromptu comeback to the global stage earlier this month.

The circuit stepped in at short notice to host this year'a Bahrain Grand Prix as a one-off substitution after the race was unable to proceed at the Bahrain International Circuit in Sakhir due to heightened geopolitical tensions and regional conflict in the Middle East.
The race weekend drew massive crowds and saw Red Bull's Max Verstappen win on wet tarmac.
708331d728ff07a5: KLANG: A window pane installer was charged at the magistrate's court with murdering an Indonesian last month.
Fauzi Mahya, 36, was accused of murdering Wijaya, who was in his 30s, at 1.20pm on Sept 25 along Jalan Shahpadu Lama, Kampung Batu Belah.
Fauzi nodded to indicate that he understood the charge when it was read out to him before magistrate Nor Azilah Mat last Friday.
No plea was recorded as murder cases fall under the jurisdiction of the High Court.

The charge, framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, carries the death penalty or a jail term of between 30 and 40 years and, if the death penalty is not imposed, at least 12 strokes of the rotan upon conviction.
The court did not grant bail and fixed Jan 12 next year for mention.
Deputy public prosecutor Ahmad Sulfie Abu Hassan prosecuted, while the accused was unrepresented.
The suspect was arrested along Jalan Harapan in Taman Sungai Kapar Indah.
Investigations found that the suspect had allegedly attacked the victim after suspecting him of having an affair with his wife.
59aec39c12d52cca: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Dental Association (MDA) has urged the government to give contract dental officers similar consideration for permanent appointments as announced for other healthcare professionals.
Under the 2027 budget tabled by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Friday, the government will offer permanent positions to more than 9,000 contract medical officers next year.

In a statement today, MDA president Dr Chong Zhen Feng said all healthcare professionals deserve fair consideration, transparent career pathways, and recognition of their contributions to the national healthcare system.
Chong said some dental officers had their contracts expire without renewal, resulting in trained dental professionals leaving the public healthcare system.

He urged the government to review the status of the affected contract dental officers and consider appropriate opportunities for permanent appointments, alongside a sustainable workforce strategy to prevent further loss of trained dental professionals from the public sector.

He said investment in training and developing dental professionals should not be overlooked, as their experience and commitment represent valuable national healthcare resources that should be retained wherever possible.

Chong said dental officers play an essential role in providing preventive and clinical oral healthcare, particularly to schoolchildren, underserved communities, and Malaysians who rely on public dental facilities.
25b4fe194905dcd7: BRUSSELS: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Monday the bloc would welcome a truce on striking energy infrastructure between Ukraine and Russia "when it holds", after US President Donald Trump announced a ceasefire.
"We welcome the energy ceasefire when it holds. We haven't yet seen that also Russia will stick to it," Kallas said at a meeting of EU foreign ministers.
Kallas said any truce needed to cover more than just oil refineries in the two countries "where Ukraine has one and Russia has plenty, so it's definitely in the benefit of the Russians."
Trump sowed confusion on Sunday by announcing an "energy ceasefire" between Ukraine and Russia that sparked astonishment in Kyiv and silence from Moscow.

Any truce appeared shaky at best as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia struck multiple Ukrainian power plants on Sunday, including one in the capital and another in Kharkiv, leading to power outages and outrage.
Kyiv's Western backers said they supported its calls for a genuine ceasefire with Russia.
Australia added its voice Monday to say it backed an "energy ceasefire", while urging Moscow to "end its unjustified and unprovoked invasion" of its neighbour.

Trump's announcement came two days after he declared a temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian diesel, prompting outrage by European allies and Kyiv, who said it would only embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin.
"If we want to end this war, the only way we can do this is putting more pressure on Russia," Kallas said, urging Washington instead to ramp up sanctions on Moscow.
EU ministers on Monday were due to add around another 1,600 individuals and entities to its own sanctions blacklist over the war on Ukraine.
The new major wave of listings will focus mainly on the Russian military and arms industry.
95e7ebf75c67cf7f: KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) is expected to receive its FA-50M light combat aircraft this month or next month, with no delays reported so far, says Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin.
He said the exact arrival date of the fighter aircraft would be announced soon.

"According to the schedule, the aircraft will arrive this month or next month; I will announce the arrival date later. So far, I have not received any information regarding a delay in the delivery of the aircraft," he told reporters after the launching ceremony of the 2026/2027 Tabung Pahlawan Campaign here today.

Also present were the Tabung Pahlawan Campaign patron Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman, Navy Chief Admiral Tan Sri Dr Zulhelmy Ithnain, and Air Force Chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris.

In May 2023, the Defence Ministry and the South Korean aerospace company signed a contract worth nearly RM4 billion for the procurement of 18 FA-50 Block 20 light combat aircraft, specifically designated as the FA-50M (Malaysia).
This variant is significantly more advanced and capable than the FA-50s operated by the Republic of Korea Air Force (ROKAF) and other nations, including Thailand, the Philippines, and Indonesia.
In June, RMAF confirmed that two FA-50M light combat aircraft were scheduled to arrive in Malaysia this month, while the remainder would be received in stages through March 2028.
76016bed8a86bcd8: KUALA LUMPUR: A miniature golden Mount Kinabalu presented by Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman to his wife, singer and actress Bella Astillah, has caught the attention of social media users after they spotted a romantic detail hidden in its design.

The wedding gift featured tiny figurines of the newlyweds, showing Syed Saddiq kneeling in front of Bella. People believe this detail represents the moment he proposed to her on Mount Kinabalu in Sabah.

One social media user was surprised by the thoughtful gesture, writing: "Such attention to detail in Syed Saddiq's wedding gifts. I thought it was just a mountain, but it turns out to symbolise her accepting his proposal!"
The golden mountain replica was given alongside a ring as part of the groom's gifts.

Syed Saddiq prepared seven trays of presents, which included insurance coverage, a postgraduate scholarship, contributions to the Employees Provident Fund's i-Simpan scheme, a home gym, a massage chair, a bicycle, a handbag, shoes, and an Umrah package.

Bella replied with nine trays of gifts for her new husband. Her presents included a ring, a pair of red-soled dress shoes, the Quran and a prayer mat, perfume, an e-book reader, spectacles, chocolates, gold, tickets to Ultraman, and a laptop bag.

The couple exchanged vows during a solemnisation ceremony at Menara Merdeka 118 on Saturday morning, conducted by former minister in charge of religious affairs Datuk Seri Dr Zulkifli Mohamad Al-Bakri.
Bella was given away by her father, Awang Astillah Abdullah, with Ustaz Syed Abdullah Syed Nordin and Ustaz Mohd Nizam Md Nor acting as official witnesses.
Syed Saddiq also presented a marriage dowry of RM500.
It was a special day for the iconic Menara Merdeka 118 as well, with Bella and Syed Saddiq becoming the first couple ever to tie the knot at the venue.
Ultimately, the symbolic mountain gift offered a sweet personal reminder of the proposal that brought the couple to this exciting new chapter of their lives.
67d450e67ef54f91: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 12 — An unidentified man was found dead early this morning, believed to have been electrocuted while attempting to steal power cables near a Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) substation in Felda Adela, near Sungai Rengit.
The deceased, who carried no identification documents, was discovered sprawled on the road shoulder by members of the public before dawn.

Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said law enforcement was alerted after receiving an emergency call through the MERS 999 response system at 6.46am regarding an unconscious individual.
“Following the information, a police team from the Kota Tinggi district police headquarters were immediately despatched to the scene to investigate.
“Initial checks revealed the male victim lying about a metre away from the TNB substation and about 20 metres from the main road," he said in a statement.
“An examination of the victim’s body found no identification documents or any initial signs indicating foul play,” he added.
Yusof said that investigators combing the scene discovered an assortment of tools suspected to have been used in the attempted cable theft.
“The items found included a small hoe measuring 45 centimetres, a cordless grinder, a steel hammer, a pipe wrench and a headlamp.”

Initial findings suggest the man died from an electric shock while attempting to cut live cabling in the vicinity. Police are currently working to ascertain his identity and confirm the official cause of death.
The body was transported to the Kota Tinggi Hospital forensic unit for a post-mortem, and police have classified the case as a sudden death report.
0c97b4b873c92372: KUALA LUMPUR: Mahkamah Tinggi menetapkan 14 Jun 2027 untuk pengurusan kes permohonan semakan kehakiman Badan Peguam bagi mencabar keputusan pihak pendakwaan menghentikan kes rasuah Yayasan Akalbudi melibatkan Timbalan Perdana Menteri Zahid Hamidi.

Hakim S Indra Nehru menetapkan tarikh berkenaan selepas peguam Abhilaash Subramaniam yang mewakili Badan Peguam, memaklumkan Zahid dan peguam negara selaku responden memperoleh kebenaran merayu dari Mahkamah Persekutuan pada 8 Okt lepas.
"Justeru, kami memohon tarikh pendengaran semakan kehakiman (di Mahkamah Tinggi), didengar selepas prosiding rayuan di Mahkamah Persekutuan selesai," katanya semasa pengurusan kes itu.
Mahkamah turut memerintahkan supaya prosiding pengurusan kes pada 14 Jun 2027 dijalankan secara e-review di hadapan timbalan pendaftar (Mahkamah Tinggi).
Abhilaash berkata, setakat ini tarikh pendengaran merit rayuan belum ditentukan serta akan mengambil masa beberapa bulan ini, termasuk untuk melengkapkan rekod rayuan dan pertukaran hujahan bertulis.

Pada prosiding itu, Peguam Persekutuan Safiyyah Omar yang mewakili peguam negara bersetuju dengan cadangan itu, manakala peguam Guok Ngek Seong yang mewakili Zahid turut memaklumkan pihaknya tidak membantah perkara itu.

Pada 8 Okt lepas, panel tiga hakim diketuai Hakim Besar Malaya Hashim Hamzah membenarkan permohonan Zahid dan peguam negara merayu terhadap keputusan Mahkamah Rayuan yang membenarkan Badan Peguam memulakan semakan kehakiman bagi mencabar keputusan pendakwaan untuk menghentikan kes rasuah Yayasan Akalbudi.

Beliau yang bersidang bersama-sama Hakim Mahkamah Persekutuan Nordin Hassan dan Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali memutuskan bahawa kes itu menimbulkan isu perlembagaan baharu yang mempunyai kepentingan awam dan memerlukan penjelasan serta keputusan muktamad oleh Mahkamah Persekutuan.

Pada 7 Mei lepas, Mahkamah Rayuan memberikan kebenaran kepada Badan Peguam untuk memulakan semakan kehakiman bagi mencabar keputusan peguam negara pada 4 Sept 2023 yang menghentikan prosiding terhadap Zahid.
Mahkamah Rayuan membatalkan keputusan Mahkamah Tinggi pada 27 Jun 2024 yang menolak permohonan Badan Peguam untuk mendapatkan kebenaran memulakan semakan kehakiman itu.
Zahid selaku responden kedua yang dicadangkan dalam prosiding semakan kehakiman itu kemudian memfailkan permohonan pada 25 Mei lepas untuk mendapatkan kebenaran merayu ke Mahkamah Persekutuan.
Peguam Negara Dusuki Mokhtar pula memfailkan permohonan berasingan untuk mendapatkan kebenaran merayu.

Dalam permohonan semakan kehakiman itu, Badan Peguam memohon deklarasi daripada Mahkamah Tinggi bahawa keputusan dibuat Hakim Mahkamah Tinggi ketika itu Collin Lawrence Sequerah, yang kini hakim Mahkamah Persekutuan, yang melepaskan dan membebaskan Ahmad Zahid daripada 47 tuduhan pecah amanah, rasuah dan pengubahan wang haram berkaitan Yayasan Akalbudi adalah terbatal dan tidak sah.

Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan pelepasan tanpa pembebasan (DNAA) itu selepas pihak pendakwaan memaklumkan mahkamah bahawa Jabatan Peguam Negara berhasrat menghentikan prosiding itu terhadap Ahmad Zahid bagi meneliti bukti-bukti baharu.
cb07f0722317909e: KUALA LUMPUR: Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin has criticised the 2027 Budget for offering numerous incentives while failing to meet the government's annual development spending commitment of RM90 billion.
He said the RM83 billion development allocation reflected the government's preference for short-term assistance over investments that could generate jobs and boost incomes.
Hamzah also questioned the 11.41 per cent increase in operating expenditure and the higher allocation for the Election Commission (EC).
"When I examined the increased allocation for the EC, I understood why so many 'sweeteners' were announced," he said during the 2027 Budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Hamzah said the government had allocated RM510 billion under the Budget, with projected revenue of RM380.8 billion and operating expenditure of RM376.8 billion, accounting for about 99 per cent of revenue.
"This means that for every RM1 in government revenue, only one sen is left for development," he said.

He reminded Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim of his commitment when tabling the Mid-Term Review of the 12th Malaysia Plan on Sept 11, 2023, to allocate at least RM90 billion annually for development expenditure.

However, Hamzah said development allocations had remained below that benchmark for four consecutive years, at RM84 billion in 2024, RM81.9 billion in 2025, RM81 billion this year and RM83 billion for 2027.
He said next year's allocation was 7.8 per cent below the RM90 billion benchmark.
Hamzah acknowledged operating expenditure was necessary to pay teachers and doctors, keep schools and hospitals running, maintain security and provide assistance to those in need.
However, he said immediate assistance alone would not be sufficient without investments to strengthen the economy and improve living standards.

Hamzah also compared the government's development approach with those of previous administrations, which he said had established economic and infrastructure foundations that continued to benefit Malaysians.

He said the 2027 Budget should be judged by the government's ability to generate sustainable economic growth and ensure prosperity was shared, rather than by the size of its allocations or the number of announcements made.
9e8de2a014370809: SHANGHAI: China's deal with the EU to curb exports of hybrid vehicles to the bloc is a fresh hit to Chinese EV makers that have ramped up hybrid shipments exempt from EU tariffs on Chinese-made EVs, as sales growth slows at home.

China's exports of hybrids to the EU's 27-member states tripled to US$7.5 billion in the first half of this year from US$2.5 billion a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data. The figure was nearly nine times the US$845 million exported in all of 2021.

Since the EU imposed additional tariffs on Chinese-made EVs in 2024, Chinese automakers have increasingly turned to plug-in hybrids, which are exempt from the extra duties. Weak charging infrastructure in parts of Europe has also supported demand for plug-in hybrids, which are marketed for their long range and strong fuel economy.
SAIC, BYD and Chery accounted for more than 90% of Chinese hybrid sales volume in the EU, while hybrids represented more than half of their European sales, according to Jefferies.
Tariff risk off, quota risk on

While European trade commissioner Maros Sefcovic said on Friday the agreement would cut the ports of "several million cars over four years", Brussels and Beijing have yet to disclose how the arrangement will be implemented.
China's commerce ministry said on Monday that the arrangement will allow continued export growth and guarantee China a quota no smaller than that granted to any other source of imports.

Investors largely viewed the agreement as a de-escalation of trade tensions and a sign that tariffs on Chinese hybrids may be off the table for now. Shares in BYD fell 1.8%, while Chery and SAIC rose 0.25% and 0.4%, respectively.
"Overall we believe it is a risk-relief rally story...as the implementation rules, volume caps, price floors, carve-outs are still pending technical negotiation," Citi analysts said.

The rapid growth of Chinese hybrid sales has increasingly challenged European manufacturers, including Volkswagen, long the region's leading plug-in hybrid seller, said Li Yanwei, an analyst at the China Automobile Dealers Association.

BYD, China's largest hybrid vehicle exporter to Europe, sold more plug-in hybrids than fully electric models in the first eight months of the year, with its Seal U SUV its best selling model, according to data compiled by Li.
Together with Chery, SAIC and Geely, the company has narrowed the gap with Volkswagen, which still commanded a 31.8% share of the EU plug-in hybrid market.
"Let's see if China honours the agreement or finds workarounds, or temporary tariff exemptions," said Michael Dunne, a consultant who closely follows the Chinese automotive industry.
Analysts said the deal is set to expedite Chinese automakers' move to increase production in Europe.
"I would expect this to strengthen the incentive for Chinese automakers to manufacture in Europe," said Bill Russo, founder of Shanghai-based consultancy Automobility.

"If access through imports becomes more constrained, investing closer to the customer becomes more attractive. But localisation requires capital...smaller players may reconsider their European ambitions."

Jefferies analysts said the deal signalled "tariff risk off, quota risk on," potentially pushing Chinese automakers towards higher-priced models, increasing pressure on German premium brands and accelerating plans to build more vehicles in Europe.
a559b64e2e00b134: ARAU, Oct 12 — Only individuals or company representatives registered as intermediaries and approved by the Road Transport Department (JPJ) will be allowed to conduct transactions on behalf of customers at all JPJ offices and branches nationwide from January 1.
JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the requirement was aimed at regulating intermediary services more systematically, transparently and with integrity.
He said registration as a JPJ-approved intermediary would open on November 1 through an online platform provided by the department.

“Each approved registered intermediary will be issued an official digital identification document bearing a serial number, valid for two years, subject to the department’s terms and regulations,” he told a press conference after inspecting the newly upgraded Perlis JPJ office counters here today.

Aedy Fadly said the implementation did not mean that JPJ had any ties, cooperation or business relationship with any registered intermediary. Registration approval also did not constitute JPJ’s endorsement, recommendation or guarantee of the services offered by the intermediary.
“JPJ will also not be responsible for any losses, fraud, additional charges or disputes arising from private transactions between customers and registered intermediaries.

“In this regard, the public is advised to remain vigilant and prioritise the department’s official channels, such as the MyJPJ application, the JPJ Public Portal, service counters and other official channels provided, to avoid any unwanted risks,” he said.

Aedy Fadly said the initiative reflected JPJ’s continued commitment to strengthening integrity, transparency and service delivery efficiency, while ensuring that customers’ interests remained a priority.

On the upgraded Perlis JPJ counters, he said the office now had a more modern, orderly and conducive environment following upgrading works under the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), which were completed in five months against the target of six months.
Aedy Fadly said the improvements were expected to benefit about 400 customers who visited the office daily, while providing staff with a more organised and comfortable working environment. — Bernama
5040cd01cfd80510: SINGAPORE, Oct 12 — Mosques across Singapore remain open for daily and Friday congregational prayers despite the haze, though non-essential outdoor activities will be suspended if air quality deteriorates to very unhealthy levels.

The Islamic Religious Council of Singapore (MUIS) in a statement today said mosques had been issued haze preparedness guidelines covering precautionary measures across different Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) levels.

The council said appropriate precautions were in place to safeguard worshippers and prayer arrangements could be adjusted according to prevailing haze conditions, available indoor facilities and national health advisories.
“Should the 24-hour PSI enter the very unhealthy range (201-300), mosques will suspend non-essential outdoor programmes and activities,” it said.

Additional measures were also being put in place to safeguard congregants, particularly the elderly and those with pre-existing health conditions, who have been advised to take extra precautions, including wearing suitable masks when attending prayers, it said.

MUIS said madrasahs and mosque-based kindergartens had been advised to implement the haze management measures in accordance with advisories issued by the Ministry of Education (MOE) and Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) respectively.

These measures include adjustments to outdoor activities, appropriate indoor arrangements and monitoring the well-being of students and staff, while parents would be informed by the respective institutions of any changes to school activities or arrangements, where necessary, it said.

“MUIS will continue to monitor the haze situation closely and work with relevant government agencies to review and adjust its measures as necessary, in line with prevailing conditions and national health advisories,” it said.
Meanwhile, Singapore’s air quality remained unhealthy on Monday, with the 24-hour PSI ranging from 104 to 147 as of 1 pm, according to the National Environment Agency (NEA).
Readings stood at 147 in the central and west regions, 133 in the east, 115 in the south and 104 in the north. — Bernama
3f9c89d928b52e19: KUALA LUMPUR: Lee Zii Jia is eager to build on his impressive run to the Arctic Open semi-finals as he prepares for tougher challenges on the European leg of the World Tour.
The independent player showed marked improvement in Vantaa, Finland, progressing from the qualifying rounds to the last four before falling to Denmark's world No. 6 Anders Antonsen.
The world No. 56 also received timely advice from close friend and eventual champion Antonsen, who encouraged him to believe in his ability and continue his comeback.
"There are a lot of positives I can take from this week — match by match, I gained a lot of confidence. I hope to bring it to the upcoming tournaments," said Zii Jia.
"Thank you for supporting me all the way. I will keep going no matter what."
Depending on withdrawals, Zii Jia could play in the Denmark Open, which begins in Odense on Tuesday.
He is listed as the fourth reserve for the Super 750 tournament.
If he misses out, the former All England champion may have to wait until the Super 500 Hylo Open in Saarbrucken from Oct 27-Nov 1 to continue building momentum.
He is also set to compete in the qualifying rounds of the Super 500 Korea Open from Oct 3-8, but is listed as fifth reserve for the Kumamoto Masters in Japan from Nov 10-15.
Nonetheless, the semi-final run is expected to help the former world No. 2 break into the top 50 when the Badminton World Federation releases its latest rankings on Tuesday.
A return to the top 50 would boost his chances of qualifying for Super 750 and Super 1000 tournaments next year.

Meanwhile, Leong Jun Hao will be looking to build on his improved performance at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games — where he stunned Indonesia's then-world No. 1 Jonatan Christie in the team event — at the Denmark Open.
World No. 30 Jun Hao faces a tricky first-round clash against Japan's world No. 16 Koki Watanabe on Tuesday.
Watanabe arrives in Odense on the back of an upset victory over Taiwan's world No. 3 Chou Tien Chen en route to the Arctic Open semi-finals.
However, Jun Hao will draw confidence from his current form and a 4-2 head-to-head record against Watanabe.
In women's singles, world No. 28 K. Letshanaa opens her campaign against Denmark's world No. 13 Line Christophersen, while world No. 37 Wong Ling Ching takes on Japan's world No. 21 Riko Gunji.
1d2c57662c5199ba: CAIRO: An Israeli strike killed at least two Palestinians in the southern Gaza Strip on Monday, health officials said.
The Israeli military said it targeted a militant in the area, without giving further information.

Late on Sunday, an Israeli airstrike hit a tent in the Mawasi area of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, killing three people, medics said. The Israeli military told Reuters on Monday they struck militants in the area.
Israel, which says Hamas has been rearming and launching attacks in violation of a ceasefire, has stepped up strikes on the group in recent weeks.
Hamas has denied trying to carry out attacks or rebuild its arsenal and accuses Israel of undermining the Gaza peace deal.

Last year's US-brokered Gaza ceasefire calls for the eventual reconstruction of the territory. But little progress has been made towards implementing a deal to end the conflict that includes terms for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.

Gaza health officials have said at least 1,400 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the October 2025 ceasefire. Israel says four of its soldiers have been killed by militants in Gaza over the same period.
8fbe23e4d30b1115: PETALING JAYA: Rakyat Malaysia dinasihat menangguhkan perjalanan ke Arab Saudi bagi tujuan ibadah umrah buat sementara waktu, kata Menteri Luar Mohamad Hasan.

Katanya, nasihat itu susulan risiko keselamatan setelah insiden Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa King Khalid di Riyadh dibom pada Sabtu lalu, mengakibatkan sekurang-kurangnya 12 terkorban, manakala 300 cedera.

"Di Makkah masih tidak ada (insiden). Cumanya ada misil yang telah meletup di Riyadh...jadi kita minta supaya rakyat Malaysia elok tangguhkan dahulu perjalanan kita ke sana (Makkah dan Madinah)," katanya menurut Bernama.
Beliau berkata demikian selepas menghadiri kebarangkatan pulang Raja Jordan Raja Abdullah II di Kompleks Bunga Raya, Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Kuala Lumpur (KLIA), Sepang.

Semalam, Kementerian Luar melaporkan tiada rakyat Malaysia terkorban atau cedera susulan serangan terbaharu di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa King Khalid di Riyadh dan insiden projektil jatuh berhampiran Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa King Fahd di Dammam, Arab Saudi, pada Sabtu.
Dalam kenyataan, Pihak Berkuasa Am Penerbangan Awam Arab Saudi memaklumkan 12 terkorban, manakala 309 lagi cedera dalam insiden serangan itu.
Empat warga Arab Saudi, dua warga Bangladesh serta masing-masing seorang warga Amerika Syarikat (AS), Mesir, Jordan, Syria, Palestin, dan Sudan dilaporkan terbunuh.
b21f9f7072141ffe: JOHOR BARU: MIC will campaign across Melaka to help Barisan Nasional (BN) secure victory in the upcoming state election, despite contesting only one seat.
MIC president Tan Sri S.A. Vigneswaran said the party would mobilise its machinery statewide, with strategic discussions underway to strengthen support among Indian voters.

He said MIC had secured nearly 49 per cent of Indian voter support in the Negri Sembilan state election despite losing both seats it contested and having no parliamentary or state assembly representation.

"Even without state government support or official allocations, we still managed to secure nearly 49 per cent of Indian voters' support. This is not easily achieved without grassroots acceptance," he said after opening the Johor MIC convention yesterday.
MIC deputy president Datuk Seri M. Saravanan and Johor MIC chairman K. Raven Kumar were also present.
Vigneswaran said BN could have an advantage in Melaka as it currently governs the state and has elected representatives and local councillors to support its campaign machinery.
He said these factors could help MIC and BN strengthen their support among Indian voters and improve their chances at the polls.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the 16th Melaka state election, with nomination on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
d38d8a9d5ea269a0: KUCHING, Oct 12 — The Sarawak government today announced a 25 per cent discount on electricity bills from January to December next year under the 2027 State Budget.

Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg, when tabling the budget at the State Legislative Assembly today, said the discount would benefit about 716,000 domestic consumers across Sarawak, at a cost of RM281 million.
The state government also announced a RM5 monthly subsidy for water bills under the free water programme, benefiting about 600,000 domestic consumers, at RM35 million.
“These initiatives reflect a government that governs with compassion, foresight, and responsibility - balancing fiscal discipline with social equity.

“By strengthening our safety nets, we strengthen the very fabric of Sarawak, ensuring that every citizen, regardless of circumstances, is given the opportunity to live with dignity, hope, and security,” he said.
The Sarawak government today unveiled a RM14.84 billion budget for 2027, themed “Together Building Prosperity and Securing Our Futures”. — Bernama
3a39e18fa8785445: BANGKOK: Singapore president Tharman Shanmugaratnam said governments across the world should address the pressing issue of how the emergence of artificial intelligence is dampening jobs demand for fresh graduates.

"There is a particular problem that we have to address very soon... and that is that, the first rung in employment, your first job upon graduation, is now seeing less demand," Shanmugaratnam told IMF and World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Monday.
"The evidence is already very clear, it's clearest in the most AI-exposed sectors."
He said the world should also avoid a situation where a "new divergence" forms between developing and advanced economies due to disruptions from AI.--REUTERS
c2aa3acd726ebe4d: KUALA LUMPUR: Sepang International Circuit (SIC) chief executive officer Azhan Shafriman Hanif is hoping Moto3 rookie Hakim Danish Ramli will rediscover his form in his remaining races this season.
SIC is banking on the 19-year-old - by far the best young rider Malaysia has had over the past decade - to pull local fans to the Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia (Oct 30-Nov 1).
Danish has notched seven top-10 finishes this season. He finished third at Mugello and went on to win his maiden GP at Brno, both in June, but his form has tapered since then.
Shafriman is keen to see him bounce back.
"I think Danish has done very well for his first year. It is very difficult to finish on the podium at this level," said Shafriman yesterday.
"He has proven himself by achieving one race win and one other podium finish this season. To achieve this in his first year is amazing.
"Performance-wise, however, he has had some ups and downs this season.
"Hopefully he will bounce back and fight hard in the remaining races."

SIC have played a huge role in Danish's development over the years as he is essentially a product of their two-wheel rider development programme, headed by Zulfahmi Khairuddin via his ZK Racing outfit.
Danish finished 14th at the Grand Prix of Indonesia after a difficult weekend at the Mandalika circuit.
He is currently ninth in the overall Moto3 standings with 107 points to his name.
Danish will next race at the Grand Prix of Australia on Oct 23-25 which is the last race before the Malaysian GP.
39e98734b5dc4943: KUALA LUMPUR: The opposition has proposed renaming Putrajaya Hospital after Dr Hasmah Ali in recognition of her contributions to the development of the country’s public healthcare system.
Opposition leader Hamzah Zainudin said Perikatan Nasional would implement the proposal if it was given the mandate to govern the country.
“We are proposing (the name change). If the current government doesn’t do it, we will do it next time,” Hamzah, the Larut MP, said when debating the 2027 budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He supported a proposal by Mas Ermieyati Samsudin (PN-Masjid Tanah) to rename the hospital after the wife of former prime minister Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
Hasmah died at the age of 100 at the National Heart Institute on Sept 28 and was laid to rest at Pusara Negara in Precinct 20, Putrajaya.
During the debate, Hamzah also urged Tabung Haji to review the minimum savings requirement of RM15,000 for depositors to qualify for the haj waiting list.
He said the requirement could burden rural residents who saved money gradually, and raised concerns that existing depositors could lose their places on the waiting list.
Hamzah also said the opposition would continue to serve as a check and balance to ensure the government acted fairly without favouring any party.
1fdf8fd5d7900235: KUALA LUMPUR: Horror features Khadam and Malam Terlarang are leading the charge at the 35th Malaysian Film Festival (FFM 35), bagging an impressive 12 nominations each and setting the stage for a spine-chilling showdown at the country's premier film awards.

Jointly produced by Astro Shaw and Infinitus Productions, Malam Terlarang secured nods in top categories including Best Film, Best Actress (Shasha Abedul), Best Supporting Actress (Datin Sofia Jane), and Most Promising Female Actor (Aila Azizul), Berita Harian reported.
The film also earned a posthumous Best Promising Director nomination for the late Nurhanisham Muhammad, affectionately known as Labu.
Its technical prowess was further recognised with nominations for Best Editing, Best Sound Design, Best Theme Song, Best Makeup, Best Costume Design, Best Poster, and Best Visual Effects.

Equally formidable is Redfilms and Komet Productions' Khadam, which captured spots in major races including Best Film, Best Director (Shamyl Othman), Best Supporting Actress (Zarra Zhaf), and Best Child Actor.

The haunting piece, created in collaboration with several co-production houses, earned additional nods for Best Original Story, Best Screenplay, Best Cinematography, Best Original Score, Best Sound Design, Best Theme Song, Best Makeup, and Best Poster.
Not far behind is Razaisyam Rashid's action-packed Tarung: Unforgiven, which racked up a solid 10 nominations to stay firmly in the title hunt.

The coveted Best Actor category promises a fierce battle among silver-screen heavyweights, pitting Shaheizy Sam (Badak) against Idan Aedan (Abah Saya Uncle Mike), Datuk Eman Manan (3 Hajat), Beto Kusyairy (Gayong 2), and Amerul Affendi (Libang Libu).

Meanwhile, the Best Actress crown sees an exciting blend of fresh faces and seasoned stars vying for glory, with Shasha Abedul (Malam Terlarang) going head-to-head against Aida Amron (Badak), Fish Liew (Payane For An Infant), Nad Zainal (Denu), and Mimi Lana (Polong).
Adding to the stakes, the grand winner of the Best Film award will walk away with a RM1 million grant under the Creative Content Fund (DKK).
This was officially announced by Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching during the recent official launch and Top 5 nomination unveiling ceremony held at Menara FINAS in Damansara.
Also present were Finas Chairman Datuk Hans Isaac and Chief Executive Officer Datuk Azmir Saifuddin Mutalib.

In keeping with tradition, FFM 35 will bestow special recognition on four legendary industry figures who have made immense contributions to Malaysian cinema: Datuk Yusof Haslam, Noorkumalasari, AR Badul, and Norlia Ghani.
Anchored by the theme Spektrum Sinema (Spectrum of Cinema), FFM 35 will take place at Istana Budaya on Nov 21 and will be broadcast live on RTM's TV2.
Multi-talented entertainer Datuk Afdlin Shauki returns to host the glamorous evening, joined by popular co-host Amelia Henderson.
2d41646971afbe0c: PUTRAJAYA: The 10-year income tax exemption and lower stamp duty on ship financing are expected to encourage more vessel registrations and investment in Malaysia's shipping industry.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said shipping companies previously had to reapply for income tax exemptions every two years, making it difficult for them to plan long-term investments.
Loke said the extended exemption, from 2027 to 2036, would give companies greater certainty to invest in new vessels and register them under the Malaysian flag.
"Many shipping companies lack the assurance and confidence to make long-term investments, such as buying ships or registering their vessels under the Malaysian flag.
"This has led shipping companies to register their vessels elsewhere, in countries offering better tax incentives, including our neighbouring countries," he told a press conference today.

Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the extension of the full income tax exemption for Malaysian shipping companies until the year of assessment 2036 when tabling 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat on Friday.

The government also introduced fixed stamp duty rates on loans for the purchase or construction of Malaysian vessels, at RM2,000 for loans of up to RM100 million and RM5,000 for loans exceeding RM100 million.
On the fixed stamp duty rates, Loke said the move would significantly reduce the cost of financing and building new vessels.
He said stamp duty was previously charged at 0.5 per cent of a vessel's value under the financing agreement.
"For a vessel worth RM100 million, the stamp duty would amount to RM500,000.
"Under the new rate, the government has set it at just RM2,000, saving shipping companies RM498,000.
"This is a substantial saving that makes it much more attractive for shipping companies," he said.
Loke said the measures would benefit not only shipping companies but also the wider maritime industry, including shipbuilding businesses in Sarawak, particularly in Sibu.
"We hope this will spur more investment in vessels and lead to more new ships being built, allowing the shipping industry to grow more rapidly," he said.
f419cdb92db3b47c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The opposition has proposed the establishment of a national entity to manage rare earth elements (REE) as a new source of national wealth in the post-petroleum era.

Opposition Leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin said the entity was necessary to prevent non-radioactive raw materials worth more than RM800 billion from being sold cheaply without value-added processing or lost through illegal mining activities.

“We therefore propose the establishment of Reenas to manage these resources in an integrated manner, from exploration to the processing of downstream products,” he said when debating the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He also said Malaysia needed to move beyond merely selling cheap electricity to foreign data centres and instead become an Asean energy powerhouse by exporting clean energy, owning regional grid infrastructure and developing energy technology.
Hamzah also urged the government to consider building nuclear power reactors to ensure a stable national electricity supply, with a clear roadmap and timeline for implementation.

In the technology sector, Hamzah suggested that the government establish a National Sovereign Data Centre and enact an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Governance Bill to mitigate the risk of breaches involving the country’s confidential information.

“Data centre usage is expected to increase 18-fold by 2040. Sensitive government data must be stored within the country, with encryption keys held by local agencies rather than relying on foreign public cloud services,” he said.

Meanwhile, he welcomed the government’s decision to continue social assistance programmes such as the Rahmah Cash Contribution (STR), Rahmah Basic Contribution (SARA) and Rahmah Sales, which he said had helped ease the people’s cost-of-living burden.

However, to address challenges arising from the implementation of the new RM2,000 minimum wage, Hamzah proposed setting up a Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Incentive Fund through the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), alongside corporate tax relief for employers who raised workers’ wages.
“Exemptions for MSMEs exist only on paper, as small employers still risk losing workers to larger companies.
“The government needs to share the cost of this transition for several years until companies’ productivity can support the new wage level,” he said. — Bernama
04f3c11e9787421d: WASHINGTON, Oct 12 — US President Donald Trump must cancel any remaining taxpayer-funded television advertisements promoting himself, a federal judge ordered yesterday, following backlash from both sides of the political divide just weeks ahead of crucial midterm elections.
According to US media reports, the Trump administration has used US$20 million (RM81.6 million) from Department of Homeland Security funds to pay for pro-Trump ads.
US District Judge Jennifer Rochon issued a temporary restraining order, preventing the administration from creating or airing such ads for 14 days.

“Defendants shall not enter into, renew, or expand any agreement authorising the development, creation, dissemination, placement, or airing of the challenged advertisements,” Rochon said in the court order.
The plaintiffs alleged the ads “exceed the purposes authorised by Congress and violate restrictions on publicity and propaganda,” according to the court order.

“We are pleased the court acted swiftly to prevent more taxpayer dollars from being used for such blatantly unlawful political propaganda,” the plaintiffs said in a statement issued by Democracy Forward, the nonprofit legal organisation that represents them.

“There is no legal justification — and no precedent — for the president to use the machinery of the government and funds set aside by Congress for other uses to influence electoral outcomes that further his own agenda.”
While Trump is not on the ballot in the November vote, he has been campaigning for Republican candidates he hopes would help the party keep control of Congress.
The White House has defended the use of taxpayer funds, saying the ads were public service announcements.
The first ad, broadcast in late September, featured a song saying Love Me while Trump proclaimed “America will never be a communist country.”
Another ad showed Trump warning of a “final battle” over black-and-white footage of him walking down a hallway, with an onscreen message saying: “Paid for by the US Government.”
The ads have drawn criticism from both Democrats and Republicans.
Democratic Senator John Hickenlooper called the ads “illegal” and “propaganda,” while some senior Republicans expressed reservations.

Trump said in a post on Truth Social last week that he and his political campaign would pay for the ads promoting himself. But the White House later told AFP that the post “was not referring to reimbursement.” — AFP

d967e178763aaef7: KUALA LUMPUR: A group representing the next of kin of 54 Malaysians missing in the Nepal floods has submitted a proposal to Bank Negara Malaysia for a structured financial protection framework to safeguard the families.
The group's spokesman, R Manivannan, said the proposal details solutions for liability defence, asset protection, and business continuity.
A separate 20-page document was presented to banking, finance, and takaful association representatives.
Following a meeting with BNM officials, Manivannan said the financial institutions have agreed in principle to halt debt collection efforts while formal guidelines are finalised.

"In principle, everyone agreed that for now, no action will be taken until an agreement is reached. They will not chase the families for payments," he told reporters outside the Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers building here today.
Under the proposed framework, the group wants banks to grant full loan moratoriums that explicitly waive accrued interest, late payment penalties, and arbitrary loan tenure extensions.
Manivannan did not disclose the proposal's other contents.

He said the status of the missing victims left their families in legal limbo and unable to access bank accounts, investments, or insurance policies because court-issued death certificates cannot be obtained without confirmed remains.

Nonetheless, he said, Nepal's recent decision to allow victims to be presumed dead 45 days after going missing, instead of the previous 12 years, would resolve the matter sooner, with the 45-day mark already passed.
5d9a40bfe54d985b: SINGAPORE: Singapore rolled out subsidies for haze-related medical treatment on Monday, and schools were closed in parts of Malaysia, as both countries grapple with persistently unhealthy air quality due to fires in nearby Indonesia.

Singapore again ranked the world's most polluted city on Monday, according to Swiss-based air quality monitor IQAir, as the fires on Borneo and Sumatra islands - intensified by a turbo-charged El Nino weather phenomenon - keep emitting toxic haze.
The fires have created severe haze locally, with tens of thousands of cases of respiratory illnesses.
In Singapore, the government activated schemes that allow citizens to receive affordable care for haze-related conditions.

The subsidies cover conditions including "allergic rhinitis, asthma, bronchitis, conjunctivitis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, upper respiratory tract infection, and their complications," the health ministry said in a statement late on Sunday.
Treatment is capped at S$10 for most eligible Singaporeans, and S$5 for senior citizens aged 67 and above.

The city-state last activated its haze subsidy scheme in 2015, when smoke from Indonesian forest fires cloaked Southeast Asia in toxic smoke for weeks, driving up illnesses and leading to school closures and flight cancellations.
In Malaysia, schools reopened Monday in most areas as air quality improved slightly, but remained closed across Johor and parts of Kuala Lumpur and Selangor.

Indonesia regularly battles wildfires during the dry season, but the fires have intensified this year because of El Nino, set to be one of the strongest since comparable records began four decades ago.
Experts have also pointed to slash-and-burn land-clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape.
The transboundary haze has also disrupted regional travel.

Malaysian low-cost carrier Firefly cancelled flights between Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport in Subang and Singapore's Seletar Airport from Saturday to Monday as a "precautionary safety measure", the airline said.

"Given the evolving weather situation, Firefly is monitoring developments closely. Further updates on flight schedules will be communicated directly to affected customers," Firefly said in a statement on Facebook.
862f53aedffc22dc: Another working week has arrived, bringing with it the chance to shine or commence career decline. The latter is the sort of thing The Register often writes about each Monday in "Who, Me?" – our reader-contributed column that shares your stories of workplace errors. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Mark," who took us deep into computing history because his story comes from his time working at the UK office of legendary mainframe maker Sperry Univac. Mark told us this was the time of "punch cards and operator scheduling of jobs and prints. Tapes and the big old disk platters." And no monitors – when a program ran, its results were sent to a printer. The inventory job ran in what Mark called "top memory," separate from the shared memory used by smaller workloads. Two printers were in place, so different workloads had their own means of creating hard copy. One of Mark's duties was working on a weekly inventory job that took five or six days to run, including the time required to print the results. Three managers supervised the important weekly job and, on this occasion, flew in from the US to observe proceedings. "Once it started printing, the main part of the job was finished and we just had to keep feeding in the 20-plus boxes of paper," Mark explained. His team therefore dedicated one printer to the job. While the mainframe and its printer churned through the inventory run, one of the smaller jobs went awry. "It generated (potentially) many more pages than it should have done, and asked if I wanted to print it all," Mark wrote. "I checked with the programmer and was given the OK to cancel the print stage, so I did." At this point, one of the printers stopped – but it was the printer working on the inventory job, not the lesser workload Mark thought he was killing. "The output was completely gone. Not even the summary pages survived." "The rest of my day was spent realizing that the three senior managers from America were unable to do anything until the job completed successfully. Next week." Mark obviously felt dreadful. "Everyone was extremely sympathetic and there was no indication of blame," he wrote, adding an ominous "but…" Have you terminated the wrong process and feared you'd terminated your career too? If so, don't stop until you click here to send your story to Who, Me? ®

400d5220761e7ba7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 12 — The Home Ministry is developing an artificial intelligence (AI)-based National Border Control System (SKSN) incorporating data analytics to strengthen surveillance and security enforcement along Malaysia’s borders.

Deputy Home Minister Datuk Seri Shamsul Anuar Nasarah said the system would serve as a smart surveillance platform, enabling real-time information sharing among enforcement agencies, detecting suspicious movement patterns and expediting responses in high-risk areas.

He said the development of SKSN was based on a feasibility study conducted by the Malaysian Institute of Public Security, including the integration of intelligence and surveillance systems through the establishment of a single command centre.

“Through SKSN, intelligence and surveillance systems will be integrated. It will combine and link information directly between enforcement agencies,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

He was responding to a supplementary question from Rushdan Rusmi (PN-Padang Besar) on the government’s master plan to establish an integrated smart border control system, particularly in Perlis, incorporating AI, smart video technology, drones, thermal sensors and intelligence databases.

On the implementation of technology-based surveillance in Perlis and along the Malaysia-Thailand border, he said the CCTV control room and Video Surveillance System (VSS) at Padang Besar Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security (ICQS) Complex were equipped with 42 cameras and 264 lights, covering a 53.3-kilometre stretch.

Shamsul Anuar said the government had also procured eight Vertical Take-Off and Landing (VTOL) drones worth RM26 million, while the supply of five Mobile Intelligence FTI units worth RM7 million was in its final stage.
“In addition, we have procured 40 units of various types of drones worth approximately RM5.2 million,” he said.

He added that the construction of a jetty and observation tower complete with CCTV cameras and drones at Batu Putih Post in Perlis, costing RM20 million, was also under way, while existing surveillance systems operated by the police were being upgraded under the Third Rolling Plan of the 13th Malaysia Plan.

Meanwhile, he said 25 illegal crossing routes had been identified in Perlis as of September 2026, while the General Operations Force (GOF) recorded seizures worth RM6.57 million along the state’s border in 2025 and RM6.27 million from January to August this year. — Bernama
698413bfce6c8a8a: BANGKOK: Strong investment in AI infrastructure is keeping global growth at around 3%, yielding major benefits for many Asian economies that supply the hardware, such as Thailand, International Monetary Fund managing director Kristalina Georgieva said on Monday.

The artificial intelligence investment boom was already delivering a "demand shock, an investment shock" that could boost growth in advanced Asian economies by a half to one full percentage point, and emerging Asian economies by 0.2 to 0.8 percentage point, she said.
"AI, love it, hate it. It's already here," Georgieva said.

"That shift into higher gear is what is keeping the world economy growing at around 3%, despite the fact we are being dragged down by the energy supply shock," she told hundreds of participants on the first day of a weeklong set of meetings of the IMF and World Bank in the Thai capital.
The IMF in July forecast global growth at 3% in 2026. It will release an updated outlook on Tuesday.

Some 18,000 people are expected to attend the meetings this week, including finance officials from the IMF's 191 members. Several ministers will skip the meeting to focus on domestic priorities, including US treasury secretary Scott Bessent and Spanish finance minister Arcadi España, sources familiar with the matter said.

Georgieva said AI amounted to a "slow-moving tsunami" that would have profound consequences for jobs, growth, education and even how governments generate revenue through taxation, given the expected shift from labor to capital.

The IMF estimates that AI could lead to 40% of jobs being augmented, downgraded or eliminated, over time, she said. An initial study showed that 10% of jobs in the US already required AI skills. While routine, repetitive jobs were shrinking, low-paying jobs were increasing in two lower-paying sectors, construction and data centers.
"It is a transformative technology. It so completely changes how we work, how we live," she said, noting that an AI assistant now gave her a 30-second message about her schedule each day.

The US, China and India are the most important producers in the AI supply chain, but many of the firms building the needed infrastructure are in Asia, Georgieva said, referencing Thailand, host of this year's annual meetings.

World Bank president Ajay Banga, who has made jobs a central focus of his presidency, said the development bank was focused on leveraging "small AI", which is not dependent on large language models, to generate enormous productivity gains for farmers, healthcare systems, educators and others in emerging markets.
Singapore's president Tharman Shanmugaratnam, speaking at the same event, said governments should address how AI was reducing job opportunities for graduates.
"There is a particular problem that we have to address very soon ... and that is that, the first rung in employment, your first job upon graduation, is now seeing less demand," he said.
He said the world should also guard against AI resulting in a "new divergence" in growth and job creation between developing and advanced economies.

"AI is going to widen the divergence if we are too passive about it," he said. "So we've got to do everything we can to first use AI to create good jobs and to create jobs that can be done well by human beings, can allow them to ride up a career ladder despite AI."
125006ae6fd5aed9: KUALA LUMPUR: The government must not burden the nation’s “golden geese” such as Petronas, Tenaga Nasional Bhd, and the Retirement Fund Inc (KWAP) with political decisions, says opposition leader Hamzah Zainudin.
Hamzah, the Larut MP, said these strategic institutions must be given room to perform their functions without having to execute government decisions that could jeopardise their financial standing.
He accused the government of leaving these institutions to bear the brunt of its political decisions.
“Let the nation’s ‘golden geese’ carry out their core operations,” he said during the debate on the 2027 budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Pointing to Petronas, Hamzah questioned the dividends paid and projected for the government, which total over RM163 billion from 2023 to 2027.
He said Petronas paid RM40 billion in 2023 and RM32 billion annually in 2024 and 2025, while dividends for 2026 and 2027 have been projected at RM27 billion and RM32 billion, respectively.
“Petronas needs large funds for its strategic investments, including phase two of the LNG Canada project, as well as developments in Suriname, Turkmenistan, and Pengerang,” he said
He also referred to the announcement of Petronas’s involvement in developing affordable housing on more than 4ha of gazetted Malay reserve land in Kuala Lumpur.

“Petronas’s job is to explore for oil and energy resources for the future. Let the decisions made by the boards of directors of our ‘golden geese’ be based on returns, not directives announced in budget speeches,” he said.

Hamzah also questioned the government’s decision to raise the electricity bill protection threshold for domestic consumers from 600kWh to 800kWh a month, saying it had caused TNB to bear RM150 million in costs.
He questioned KWAP’s involvement in several development initiatives, which he said was inappropriate as the institution was not a bank. “Its mandate is to provide safe returns for retirees,” he said.

aaf4f892f2ce2a66: TOKYO: French defence contractor Thales will establish a maintenance and operational support base in Japan in what is seen as the first such move by a foreign firm in the country, a report said Monday.
Chairman and CEO Patrice Caine told the Nikkei business daily that the base "will mark a milestone toward Thales's long-term engagement in Japan".
It is believed to be the first time a foreign defence company has established a dedicated base in Japan for the maintenance and operation of Japanese defence equipment, the Nikkei said.
It added that Thales may also expand its Japan-based business to civilian use in the future.

The report comes as Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi boosts defence spending in the face of China's rapid military expansion and an unpredictable North Korea, moving away from the traditional pacifist stance that limited the use of force to self-defence.
Thales already supplies equipment to Japan's Self-Defense Forces, the Nikkei said.

8b2f8d69421730b4: KUALA LUMPUR: The air force is expected to receive the FA-50M light combat aircraft manufactured by Korea Aerospace Industries according to schedule, says defence minister Khaled Nordin.
Khaled said the exact arrival date of the fighter aircraft would be announced soon.

"According to the schedule, the aircraft will arrive this month or next month – I will announce the arrival date later. So far, I have not received any information regarding a delay in the delivery of the aircraft," he told reporters after the launch of the Warriors' Fund Campaign 2026/2027 here today.
In May 2023, the ministry and Korea Aerospace signed a contract worth nearly RM4 billion for 18 FA-50 Block 20 light combat aircraft, specifically designated as the FA-50M (Malaysia).
This variant is significantly more advanced and capable than the FA-50s operated by the Korean air force and other nations, including Thailand, the Philippines and Indonesia.

bec90d8ed927da02: PETALING JAYA: Iskandar Investment Berhad (IIB) mahu mempercepat pelaksanaan pelaburan di Johor supaya komitmen pelabur dapat diterjemahkan kepada operasi perniagaan sebenar yang mewujudkan pekerjaan dan mengukuhkan ekonomi tempatan.

Presiden dan Ketua Pegawai Eksekutifnya Idzham Mohd Hashim berkata langkah diumumkan dalam Belanjawan 2027, termasuk insentif cukai, pembangunan bakat dan penambahbaikan pengangkutan, mampu meningkatkan daya tarikan Johor sebagai destinasi pelaburan bernilai tinggi.
“Belanjawan 2027 menjadikan Johor lebih menarik sebagai destinasi pelaburan. Insentifnya jelas, agenda kesalinghubungan terus bergerak dan penekanan terhadap bakat adalah tepat.

“Tanggungjawab kami ialah mempercepat proses daripada minat dan komitmen pelabur kepada operasi sebenar yang menggaji rakyat Malaysia, mengukuhkan rantaian tempatan dan mencipta nilai berkekalan,” katanya dalam kenyataan.
Antara langkah diumumkan ialah penambahbaikan insentif Hab Perkhidmatan Global (GSH) yang menawarkan kadar cukai 5% ke atas pendapatan layak bagi syarikat baharu yang memenuhi syarat.
Idzham berkata insentif itu berpotensi menarik lebih banyak syarikat antarabangsa menjalankan operasi serantau di Malaysia, termasuk dalam bidang kewangan, teknologi, pengurusan data dan perniagaan.

Menurutnya, langkah itu turut menyokong perkembangan sektor perkhidmatan perniagaan global (GBS) di Medini serta Zon Ekonomi Khas Johor-Singapura (JS-SEZ), yang merekodkan pelaburan RM132 bilion antara 2025 hingga Jun 2026.

Beliau berkata pelancaran pelan induk dan rangka tindakan JS-SEZ yang dirancang menjelang akhir tahun ini juga dijangka memberikan hala tuju lebih jelas kepada syarikat yang mahu memulakan atau mengembangkan operasi di Johor.

Dalam aspek pekerjaan, Idzham berkata pembangunan bakat perlu seiring dengan keperluan industri bagi memastikan pelaburan baharu dapat menghasilkan peluang kerjaya berkualiti dan meningkatkan pendapatan rakyat.

“Latihan mesti bergerak seiring dengan keperluan industri. Majikan perlu membantu menjelaskan kemahiran yang mereka perlukan, manakala institusi pendidikan dan agensi bakat perlu menyediakan laluan kerjaya yang jelas,” katanya.

Johor menerusi Pelan Transformasi Ekonominya menyasarkan lebih 200,000 pekerjaan baharu berkualiti menjelang 2030, manakala Belanjawan 2027 memperuntukkan RM8 bilion bagi pendidikan dan latihan teknikal dan vokasional (TVET) serta RM3 bilion melalui HRD Corp di seluruh negara.
